title: Prayer in the Church
definition: Prayer in the Church is the gathered and continual dependence of God's people on the Father through Christ by the Holy Spirit.
summary: Prayer in the Church is the congregation's shared dependence on God for mercy, wisdom, power, healing, mission, and perseverance.
christFocus: Jesus Christ gives His people access to the Father and intercedes for them as they pray.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on corporate dependence. When the Church prays together, it confesses that ministry cannot be sustained by planning, skill, or personality alone. Prayer unites the congregation before God and brings needs, mission, leaders, suffering, and spiritual battles under His care.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because churches can become active without being dependent. Corporate prayer exposes self-sufficiency and invites the congregation to seek the Lord together. It also teaches believers to carry one another's burdens before the throne of grace.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Participate in church prayer as ministry, not filler. Pray for specific people, leaders, mission work, holiness, and the suffering. Help cultivate a church culture where dependence on God is normal and visible.
